## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Edge, motion and sky features of an AXI4-Stream video (24-bit
pixels {B, G, R}, tuser = start of frame, tlast = end of line) for
object detectors. Version 2.0.0. A tap on the accepted beats of s_axis
(tvalid & tready; it never stalls the stream): every beat is forwarded
on m_axis two clocks later (tvalid one clock per beat; m_axis.tready is
not used) with feat_o, the feature bits of that pixel ([0] edge, [1]
motion; 0 while the frame is not processed), so object_tracker
detectors watching m_axis get the bits with their beat. Golden model:
ip/video/feature_detect/model/feature_detect_model.py (its header
defines every bit and register; tb/python compares them).
  - A frame is processed when CTRL.EN is set at its start; CTRL, EDGE,
    MOTION, SHIFT and SKY_CFG are taken at the frame start. FRAME_SIZE
    must be the frame's size (the frame end and the cells come from it).
  - Luma Y = (R + 2 G + B) / 4: a shift-add approximation of BT.601 luma
    (ITU-R BT.601-7: 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B); blue weighs 0.25
    instead of 0.114, so blue objects look brighter to the tests.
  - Edge (feat_o[0]): the Sobel |Gx| + |Gy| of the 3 x 3 window ending
    at the pixel (rows y - 2 .. y, columns x - 2 .. x; x, y >= 2) above
    EDGE.THRESH, filled along the line over EDGE.SPAN pixels.
  - Motion (feat_o[1]): cells of 2^CELL_LOG2 pixels square (cw = width >>
    CELL_LOG2 by ch = height >> CELL_LOG2); per cell the lowest / highest
    luma x 16 in two background banks (one read during a frame, the
    other written; they swap at the frame end); a pixel moves when the
    background is valid, its source cell (cx - sx, cy - sy) is in the
    frame and its luma is below lo / 16 - MOTION.THRESH or above hi /
    16 + MOTION.THRESH; filled over MOTION.SPAN. At its last pixel each
    cell is written: old + (new - old) >>> MOTION.RATE of its source,
    or the new values without a valid source. The first frame after a
    restart only fills the background.
  - Camera shift: column / row luma profiles per cell column / cell row
    in three rotating banks; after a frame with a previous one a search
    (per axis the shift -SHIFT_MAX .. SHIFT_MAX with the lowest sum of
    |cur[i] - prev[i - s]| over i = SHIFT_MAX .. n - 1 - SHIFT_MAX; 0
    first, a later shift only when strictly lower; one term per clock,
    STATUS.BUSY) runs during the next frame -> SHIFT_EST; with
    CTRL.AUTO_SHIFT a frame uses the estimate of the search that ended
    two frames before it (the search after frame N, frame N + 2), else
    SHIFT.
  - Sky: per column group of 2^SKY_CFG.SHIFT pixels (32 groups) the lines
    from the top to its first pixel with the edge bit or a luma below
    SKY_CFG.Y_MIN (the frame height when none) -> SKY[0..31].
  - Restart (a CTRL write with RESTART, or a FRAME_SIZE write): at the
    next frame start the background, profiles and shift start again.
  - Per frame EDGE_COUNT, MOTION_COUNT, FRAMES; done_o pulses once a
    frame's results and its shift search are complete.
Memories: the luma line buffer, the background banks and the column
profiles are read with a registered read (block RAM); cell addresses
are counted, not multiplied. Limits: frames of at least SHIFT_MAX + 2
cells each way and more beats than the search's clocks (about (2
SHIFT_MAX + 1) (cw + ch)); CELL_LOG2 >= 1.
Registers on the cfg_* / sts_* ports; feature_detect_top.sv is the block
with its AXI4-Lite register map (src/include/feature_detect_regs.sv,
ADDR_W = 8): ID "FEAT" / VERSION / DATE at 0x00-0x08, CTRL 0x18,
FRAME_SIZE 0x1C, EDGE 0x20, MOTION 0x24, SHIFT 0x28, SHIFT_EST 0x2C,
STATUS 0x30, FRAMES 0x34, EDGE_COUNT 0x38, MOTION_COUNT 0x3C,
SHIFT_USED 0x40, SKY_CFG 0x44, SKY 0x80 + 4 i.
Clock - clk (pixel clock). Reset - synchronous active low rst_n.

feature_detect with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the
block designs and testbenches instantiate: the register map
feature_detect_regs (u_regs, src/include/feature_detect_regs.sv, ID
"FEAT", VERSION and DATE at 0x00-0x08, the registers from 0x10) and the
logic feature_detect (u_core, src/feature_detect.sv), joined by the
register interface feature_detect_regs_if (u_regs_if). Generated by
ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py from feature_detect_regs.json and the ports of
feature_detect: regenerate after changing either. Clock - clk. Reset -
synchronous active low rst_n.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - feature_detect (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] R. C. Gonzalez, R. E. Woods, "Digital Image Processing", 4th ed., Pearson 2018, ch.
//   3.4-3.6 (spatial correlation / convolution, Gaussian / binomial smoothing, unsharp masking
//   and highboost g = f + k (f - f_blur), Sobel gradient |Gx| + |Gy|); unsharp summary
//   https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/UNSHARP_MASK.html
//   [2] I. Haritaoglu, D. Harwood, L. S. Davis, "W4: Real-time surveillance of people and their
//   activities", IEEE PAMI 22(8), 2000, doi:10.1109/34.868683 (background as per-pixel minimum
//   / maximum intensity, foreground outside it)
//   [3] K. Ratakonda, "Real-time digital video stabilization for multi-media applications",
//   ISCAS 1998 vol. 4 pp. 69-72 (row / column integral projections, 1-D shift search by minimum
//   SAD)
//   [4] ITU-R BT.601-7 (2011) https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.601 and BT.709-6 (2015)
//   https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.709 - Kr/Kb 0.299/0.114 and 0.2126/0.0722, 8-bit Y = 16 +
//   219 E'Y, C = 128 + 224 E'C; scaled equations in Linux V4L2 colorspaces
//   https://docs.kernel.org/7.1/_sources/userspace-api/media/v4l/colorspaces-details.rst.txt
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   Edges: Sobel gradient with |Gx| + |Gy| as the magnitude approximation (Gonzalez & Woods
//   10.2). Motion: W4 background = per-pixel (here per-cell) minimum / maximum intensity, a
//   pixel is foreground outside [min - t, max + t]. Global (camera) shift: integral projections
//   of rows and columns matched by minimum SAD (Ratakonda 1998). Luma: BT.601 Y = 0.299 R +
//   0.587 G + 0.114 B.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: 3x3 Sobel with L1 magnitude, W4-style min / max background with threshold and slow
//   update, projection-profile shift search by minimum SAD. Differs: luma is (R + 2G + B) / 4 =
//   0.25 R + 0.5 G + 0.25 B, not BT.601 (blue weighted 0.25 instead of 0.114), so blue objects
//   look brighter to the edge and motion tests than in a standard luma image.
// RESOLVED(REF-FEATURE_DETECT-1) [LOW] Luma weights. Resolution: 2026-10-21: Y = (R + 2G + B) / 4
//   is kept (shift-add, no multipliers); the feature_detect.sv header states that it approximates
//   BT.601 luma (ITU-R BT.601-7) and that blue weighs 0.25 instead of 0.114; the golden model uses
//   the same luma (pixel.luma) and tb/python checks every pixel.
```

### Register map (from `feature_detect_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "FEAT" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x18 | CTRL | RW | 0 | control | EN[0] enable (follow the stream); EDGE_EN[1] edge bit on; MOTION_EN[2] motion bit on; AUTO_SHIFT[3] use the searched camera shift (else SHIFT); RESTART[4] write 1: background, profiles and shift start again (the next frame fills the background) |
| 0x1C | FRAME_SIZE | RW | 0 | frame size | WIDTH[15:0] width; HEIGHT[31:16] height |
| 0x20 | EDGE | RW | 0x00080080 | edge detector | THRESH[10:0] Sobel \|Gx\| + \|Gy\| above this: an edge; SPAN[19:16] an edge in the last SPAN pixels of the line sets the bit (0 or 1: the pixel only) |
| 0x24 | MOTION | RW | 0x00002214 | motion detector | THRESH[7:0] luma beyond the background cell's range by more than this: moving; SPAN[11:8] fill along the line, as EDGE.SPAN; RATE[14:12] background moves 1 / 2^RATE of the way to each frame |
| 0x28 | SHIFT | RW | 0 | camera shift used without AUTO_SHIFT (cells, taken at the frame start) | X[7:0] columns (signed): content moved right; Y[15:8] lines (signed): content moved down |
| 0x2C | SHIFT_EST | RO | 0 | camera shift found by the last search (cells) | X[7:0] columns (signed); Y[15:8] lines (signed) |
| 0x30 | STATUS | RO | 0 | state | IN_FRAME[0] in a frame; BG_VALID[1] background valid (motion detected); BUSY[2] shift search running; FRAMES[31:16] FRAMES[15:0] |
| 0x34 | FRAMES | RO | 0 | frames seen | - |
| 0x38 | EDGE_COUNT | RO | 0 | pixels with the edge bit in the last frame | - |
| 0x3C | MOTION_COUNT | RO | 0 | pixels with the motion bit in the last frame | - |
| 0x40 | SHIFT_USED | RO | 0 | camera shift in effect for the current / last frame (cells) | X[7:0] columns (signed); Y[15:8] lines (signed) |
| 0x44 | SKY_CFG | RW | 0 | sky profile: column groups of 2**SHIFT pixels (group g = x >> SHIFT, at most 32 groups); a sky pixel has no edge and luma Y_MIN or more | SHIFT[3:0] log2 of the group width; Y_MIN[15:8] least luma (R + 2G + B) / 4 of a sky pixel (a dark smooth road or ceiling is not sky) |
| 0x80 + 4 i (i < 32) | SKY | RO | 0 | sky profile of the last frame: lines from the top of column group i down to its first pixel that is not sky (the frame height: all sky); a plane in the sky is the first thing below it | - |

The block is generated, not hand-written: write the JSON above and run `python3 ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py ip/video/feature_detect/src/include/feature_detect_regs.json`, which also emits the C header and Markdown documentation. Extend the generator rather than editing its output.


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 4668 LUTs, 2214 flip-flops, 1 DSP48E1, 220 RAMB36E1, 5 RAMB18E1. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for feature_detect: the structural
checks (ID block, registers, beats forwarded on m_axis in order with
stalls of the observed stream, disable, FRAMES / done_o, edges counted,
RESTART timing). axis_frame_bfm sends the frames; tready of the observed
stream, which feature_detect only watches, is driven here. Every pixel's
feature bits and every register are compared with the golden model by
the cocotb test tb/python/feature_detect_tb.py. Prints TEST PASSED on
success; +vcd dumps feature_detect_tb.vcd. The test tasks are in
tests/feature_detect_tests.sv (`included).
```

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh feature_detect --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `feature_detect_tb` | `test_id_block` | ID "FEAT", VERSION ("d.dd") and DATE (BCD mm/dd/yyyy) at the base address, read only (SLVERR); the rest of the map from 0x10 |
| `feature_detect_tb` | `test_registers` | Reset values (EDGE 0x00080080, MOTION 0x00002214, STATUS, FRAMES) and read back |
| `feature_detect_tb` | `test_forward` | CTRL.EN = 0: every beat forwarded, no feature bit, no frame counted; EN = 1 with stalls: forwarded, FRAMES and done_o count the frame, a square gives edges (EDGE_COUNT), none at threshold 2040 |
| `feature_detect_tb` | `test_restart` | The background is valid after a frame; a RESTART written between frames acts at the next frame start (STATUS.BG_VALID low during that frame, valid again after it) |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C video/feature_detect test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
